ASTROCRASH — Kevin Ridley, 1984

This program comes from the Spectrum Show AstroCrash collection. We kept the original AstroCrash.z80 snapshot and the supplied tape exports unchanged. The 177-line AstroCrash.bas listing was decoded from AstroCrash.tzx with the ZX-UX ROM LLIST reader.

The program describes a rocket in a meteor storm. Its on-screen instructions say to destroy 50 meteors. Turning, moving, firing and hitting meteors use power. The original source credits Kevin Ridley and names Paul Jenkins for a later typed and repaired version.

We opened the original snapshot in Fuse 48K, advanced through the instructions, entered Y to play, then pressed X, Space, Enter and Z. The real game view changed during these actions. Meteors also move without player input, so the pictures do not prove the rocket followed an exact path or that a shot hit a meteor. No winning round was observed. The sky remains rather busy.

The PNGs in SCREENSHOTS are from that live Fuse session. REPLAY.sh repeats the opening and key sequence. It requires Fuse SDL, Xvfb, Python 3, Pillow and python-xlib. No native program was made.
